t: What Scientific Hypothesis Registry Is All About
title: What Scientific Hypothesis Registry Is All About
description: A scientific hypothesis is a testable explanation that makes falsifiable predictions. Strong hypotheses specify measurable outcomes in advance: the Higgs mechanism predicted a scalar boson near 125 GeV, confirmed in 2012. Hypotheses live or die by prediction: general relativity predicted starlight bending by 1.75 arcseconds at the solar limb, confirmed by Eddington in 1919. This database is the complete hypothesis: full records with definitions, key facts, procedures, and runnable demo programs, organized on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced.

t: Core Vocabulary of Scientific Hypothesis Registry
title: Core Vocabulary of Scientific Hypothesis Registry
description: Every field has its own language. These are the working terms of Scientific Hypothesis Registry — learn them first and every later record reads faster: falsifiability: a hypothesis must forbid some possible observation, or it is not scientific; null hypothesis: the default assumption of no effect, which experiments try to reject; p-value: probability of data this surprising if the null were true; prior: belief about a hypothesis before new evidence.
definition: The working vocabulary of Scientific Hypothesis Registry: the terms practitioners actually use.
key_points: falsifiability: a hypothesis must forbid some possible observation, or it is not scientific
null hypothesis: the default assumption of no effect, which experiments try to reject
p-value: probability of data this surprising if the null were true
prior: belief about a hypothesis before new evidence
likelihood: probability of the evidence if the hypothesis were true
auxiliary hypothesis: background assumption bundled into a test
how_it_works: Read each term and definition twice.
Use three terms in a sentence of your own.
Quiz yourself with the demo program.
Add new terms as you meet them.
